17 Influence of drugs in road traffic collisions
The consumption of illegal drugs is related to many of the most serious accidents. A person driving under the influence of drugs puts all those around him/her at serious risk of accidents.
One of the effects of drugs is that risk perception decreases and some drugs can cause the driver to have an incorrect perception of time and space. The consumption of drugs will never improve reaction time. For people who take drugs and drive, the probability of having an accident is greater. It is forbidden to drive any vehicle with presence of drugs in the body. Substances excluded are those used under medical prescription and for therapeutic purposes, provided that the driver is able to manage the vehicle and drive with diligence, precaution and without distractions.
Driving with drugs present in the body may result in the loss of 6 points.

DISTRACTIONS    
   
8.1 Circumstances of collisions due to phone use
Research indicates that there are four moments especially dangerous when using a mobile phone whilst driving:
When a call is received, as the sound of the phone may surprise the driver and when attempts are made to answer both cause distractions. Therefore it is desirable to turn off or silence the phone whilst driving.
When dialling or sending a message. To dial a phone number takes between 5 and 10 seconds and sending a long message takes a greater time during which control of the vehicle and attention is reduced or lost.
(Página 36 del manual 'Learning to drive')

DISTRACTIONS    
   
8.1 Circumstances of collisions due to phone use
Research indicates that there are four moments especially dangerous when using a mobile phone whilst driving:
Whilst speaking. Even with a hand free set, the first minute and a half of the conversation requires a high degree of focus and attention. After this time the driver fails to receive 40% of road signals and information and their average speed is reduced by 12% however they also take longer to react to a hazard or event.
When terminating a call. The effect is worsened when the driver continues to think about the conversation. Normally, it takes some time for the driver’ concentration to return fully to driving and monitoring the traffic and environment.

4 Night time driving
Vision, the ability to see, is always reduced during the hours of darkness, compared with during the day light hours. Therefore driving at night is much more dangerous than driving during the day. This is because:
The main beam or dipped (low beam) headlights illuminate a smaller zone compared with what you are able to see during the day and with the natural daylight.
Distances, people, objects and vehicles are appraised wrongly and interpreted and perceived differently during the hours of darkness as compared with during the daylight hours.
There is increased glare –which in itself is hazardous and increases the potential for danger.   
 
(Página 226 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
FACTORS THAT AFFECT PHYSICAL CAPABILITIES
 
11.1 Causes of drowsiness
The use of stimulants and sedatives. Some substances, like alcohol or certain medicines, can have a sedative effect. Large meals that
are rich in fats may also promote the need for sleep. Light stimulants (coffee, tea, some energy drinks etc.,) may be useful in the short term, but the effects can wear off suddenly, catching the driver off guard.
Individual differences. Some people are more awake in the morning and may become sleepier in the afternoon, whilst others are not so affected by the lack of sleep, medication or monotony when driving.
(Página 39 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Use of the road
 
1 Road positioning
As a general rule, vehicles will drive on the right and as close as possible to the edge of the road, keeping a lateral separation that is large enough to safely pass by other vehicles.
This regulation will be particularly applicable on curves and changes of gradient with reduced visibility. In these cases, even when there is no sign expressly delimiting directions, all drivers must leave the half of the roadway that is for the opposite direction completely free, except when overtaking.
(Página 161 del manual 'Learning to drive')
